4. Whether petitioner sustained injuries due to his own fault and overload of his scooter, if so, its effect?
16. Both these issues are inter related and intertwined and are thus taken together.
PW1 by way of affidavit stated that on 06.02.2004 at about 3.30 p.m., he was going towards Shakarpur from Kalyanpuri.

As he reached on Patparganj road, in front of Mother Dairy, a bus bearing No. DL 1PA 0477, driven by respondent no.1 at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, hit his Scooter from behind and because of impact, he fell down on road and sustained fracture in his both hands and multiple injuries upon his face and legs.

He denied the suggestion that his scooter MAC Petition No. 25/13 Darshan Singh V/s. Ramesh Chander & Ors. Page : 6/17 was overloaded by replying that it was not practicable to load goods on scooter as he was coming after taking some orders.
17.Driver/respondent no.4 has admitted of FIR having registered against him and criminal case pending before Ld. MM.
It was a broad day light accident.
The Driver of Bus ought to have exercised much care and prudence while driving heavy vehicle like bus and he should have maintained proper distance.
There is nothing in support of the plea taken by defence that accident was caused because Scooter of petitioner was overloaded.
The offending bus hit the scooter from behind, a fact, which itself shows the driver failing in taking due care to safety of life and property of others while driving the bus on road.
The facts are supported and corroborated by IO of the case who had conducted the investigation in the matter.

In Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors. 1999 ACJ 634, the Hon'ble Guwahati High Court has observed as under :
"In deciding a matter tribunal should bear in mind the caution struck by the Apex Court that a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is neither a criminal case nor a civil case.

sentences.text: In a criminal case in order to have conviction, the matter is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt and in a civil case the matter is to be decided on the basis of preponderance of evidence, but in a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in a civil case.
No doubt before the tribunal there must be some material on the basis of which the tribunal can arrive or MAC Petition No. 25/13 Darshan Singh V/s. Ramesh Chander & Ors.

Hon'ble Supreme Court enumerated the principles for granting the compensation payable to road traffic accident victims.

In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar &
Anr., MANU/SC/1018/2010, Civil Appeal No. 8981/2010 decided on 18.10.2010, following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims :
i) The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

sentences.text: Page : 10/17 ii) Compensation payable in injury cases is payable under two heads.
They are pecuniary damages (special damages) and non pecuniary damages.

Pecuniary damages have three sub heads which are :
(i) expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) (a) Loss of earning (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising of loss of earning during the period of treatment and (b)
loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (iii) Future medical expenses.

Non pecuniary damages (General Damage) are (iv) damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries (v) loss of amenities and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and (vi) loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
iii) In routine personal injury cases compensation is awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation is granted under any of the heads (ii) (b), (iii) and (vi)
relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospectus of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

27.It is well settled that a victim of an accident has to be compensated in terms of money even if gratuitous services are rendered by a family member.

In Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Vs.
Lalita, AIR 1981 Delhi 558, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that there cannot be any deduction if domestic help is obtained from a family member.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court has observed as under : "...........A wrong doer cannot take advantage of this 'domestic element'.
If the mother renders service to her, instead of a nurse, it is right and just that she should recover compensation for the value of the services that the mother has rendered to her.
Mother's services were necessitated by the wrong doing and the injured should be compensated for it.
(Cunnigharn v. Harrison 3 All E.R. 463).
The services of a wife and mother are worth more than those of a housekeeper because she is in constant attendance and does many more things than a housekeeper.

(Regan v. Williamson (1976)
2 All E.R. 241)."

opennyai_summary.facts:
Initially, injured Darshan Singh had filed the Claim Petition under section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act
claiming compensation for the injuries caused in a road side accident which occurred on
06.02.2004.
2.
Predecessor was set aside with directions to pass a fresh Award after giving an opportunity to the LRs of the injured Late Sh. Darshan Singh for their impleadment.
As a result of impact, injured fell down on road and sustained multiple injuries all over his body.
The said Award was set aside by Hon'ble High Court Delhi vide order dated 15.01.2013 observing that injured Darshan Singh had passed away on 11.08.2009 and the Award was passed in favour of a dead person, which was unsustainable under law.
6. After hearing parties on the application u/o. 22 Rule 3 (1) CPC r/w. Section 151 CPC filed on behalf of Legal Representative of the deceased, all the LRs of the deceased were brought on record.
opennyai_summary.issue:
, perused the entire material carefully in the light of relevant statutory provisions of law and my observations on the issues are as follows : ISSUES NO. 1 & 4 :
1. Whether the injuries sustained by the petitioner were caused due to rash and negligent driving of bus no. DL 1 PA 0477 by Sh. Titu S/o. Sh. Nemchand, owned by respondent no. 1 and insured with respondent no. 2?

3
4. Whether petitioner sustained injuries due to his own fault and overload of his scooter, if so, its effect?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It was a broad day light accident.
There is nothing in support of the plea taken by defence that accident was caused because Scooter of petitioner was overloaded.
The offending bus hit the scooter from behind, a fact, which itself shows the driver failing in taking due care to safety of life and property of others while driving the bus on road.
The facts are supported and corroborated by IO of the case who had conducted the investigation in the matter.
In Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors. 1999 ACJ 634, the Hon'ble Guwahati High Court has observed as under :
"In deciding a matter tribunal should bear in mind the caution struck by the Apex Court that a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is neither a criminal case nor a civil case.
After all, it is a summary inquiry and this is a legislation for the welfare of the society."
18.In the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Vijay Laxmi & Ors.
In Bimla Devi and Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors., (2009)
13 SC 530, the Supreme Court held that in a petition under Section 166 of the Act, the petitioners were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition under the Motor Vehicles Act.
19.The report in Bimla Devi (Supra) was relied on by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in its later judgments in Parmeshwari v. Amir Chand (2011) 11 SCC 635 and Kusum Lata v. Satbir, (2011) 3 SCC 646."
20.In the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pushpa Rana & Ors. : 2009 ACJ 287
, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that :

In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar &
Anr., MANU/SC/1018/2010, Civil Appeal No. 8981/2010 decided on 18.10.2010, following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims :
i) The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner.
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation is granted under any of the heads (ii) (b), (iii) and (vi)
relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospectus of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
